newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangxi Copper seen gaining on debut.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper seen gaining on debut.

text.p: Shares of Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd are expected to rise after the company debuts on Thursday on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, analysts said on Tuesday, but they also warned of risks from copper price fluctuations.

Analysts said that the strong performances of other recent new listings on the exchange and an oversubscription for new shares of Jiangxi Copper indicated the stock should gain from the issue price of HK$2.55 per share.
"It is expected to gain good support above the issue price taking into account of its subscription response," said Ben Tam, analyst at Yamaichi International.
Analysts said the company's strategy of expanding mining reserves through acquisitions and increasing efficiency should reduce the risk of a slowdown in output and sustain growth.

Jiangxi Copper offered 628.212 million H shares in a global flotation. Of the total, 62.822 million H shares or 10 percent were offered for public subscription in Hong Kong and were subscribed by 32.9 times.
The company shares will have a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange.
However, some analysts said the major risk for the company was its high sensitivity to copper prices.
"Its revenue can be affected by the volatile copper price," said Kelvin Tang, analyst at Impac Asset Management.
Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities, said the company's earnings were "not that promising" and its earnings growth could be hard to predict.
Jiangxi Copper is engaged in copper mining, milling, smelting and refining facilities in northeastern Jiangxi province in China.

The company's parent Jiangxi Copper Co is controlled by China National Non-Ferrous Metals Corp which was set up by the State Council to manage and control a portion of the non-ferrous metals industry in China.
